 I coulda been somebody
 Well, another campaign season come and gone and once again, I didn’t get elected to anything. It’s too bad, because I was ready. I’ve got this new suit I never wear, I’ve been practicing my handshakes and pasted-on smiles and I can spout empty rhetoric with the best of them. It’s a real bummer because that suit cost me like 30 bucks and now it just hangs there in my closet. A few people tell me they wrote me in for the big Senate gig, but there just weren’t enough to get me in. Pity. All I needed to do was Google “what does a senator do?” and I would have been good to go.
 Same ol’, same ol’
 Would it be weird to secretly hope certain candidates get reelected just so I don’t have to change anything in my contact list? I really hate the contact manager on my phone, so sweeping changes are rough. I mean, we’re teetering toward societal collapse no matter who lands in what office, so why should I have to suffer with phone nonsense when I could be stocking up on Band-Aids, beans and bullets?
 ‘Tis the season
 If a week after Election Day there are still campaign signs littering the roadsides, I say there should be some kind of open season for us common folk to … let’s just say, clean them up. It would be a great way to use your leftover fireworks or your riding lawn mower before you pack it away for the winter. Fun, right? This is exactly the kind of thing we’d be getting if you people had been wise enough to elect me to that Senate gig.
 On your marks
 When I heard there was going to be a runoff election in December to decide Lewiston’s mayoral race, I got wicked excited. Thought they would be literally running a foot race through Kennedy Park or something. Maybe make it an obstacle course and require the candidates to carry those gigantic trash bins they cursed us with. A few laps across the canals, a dramatic breaking of the finish line tape and you’re done! Welcome aboard, Mr. Mayor. And with that win in hand, candidate A or B gains the right to be blamed for every single thing that goes on in the city for the next two years.
 75 degrees? In November?
 Well, that was weird. I went outside in my base layers, merino socks, and gloves thick enough for a moon landing and then almost dropped from heat exhaustion in my driveway. Now I’m all about shorts, Hawaiian shirts and thongs and in two days they’ll probably drag me in with frostbite. November toys with me.
 Oh, you
 When I say “thongs,” you understand I’m talking about a certain style of sandals, right? Don’t get any weird ideas.
 Mark LaFlamme is an award-winning Sun Journal reporter and columnist. He’s covered the nighttime police beat since 1994, which is just grand because he doesn’t like getting out of bed before noon. He is the author of eight published novels and rides a dual sport motorcycle everywhere he goes. Unless it’s winter, in which case he just sulks a lot.
